sn.e: A chair of mine broke.
I need something to fix it.
I go to the hardware shop.
Inside there is everything.
There are nails in many sizes.
There are screws, hammers and paint.

sn.s: Hay cosas que no sé cómo se llaman.
sn.e: There are things I do not know the name of.

sn.s: Y justo esa cosa es la que necesito.
sn.e: And that is exactly the thing I need.
"Buenas," I say.
"Buenas. What are you after?"
I do not know the word.
I stay quiet for a moment.
Then I start to describe it.

sn.s: "Es una cosa de metal", digo yo.
sn.e: "It is a metal thing," I say.
"It is small, about this size."

sn.s: Le enseño el tamaño con los dedos.
sn.e: I show him the size with my fingers.
"It is for joining two pieces of wood."
"And you put it in with a hammer."
The man does not hesitate.
"A nail," he says.
"A nail," I repeat.
"What size do you want?"

sn.s: Le enseño el tamaño otra vez.
sn.e: I show him the size again.

sn.s: Me da una bolsa de clavos.
sn.e: He gives me a bag of nails.
Then I need another thing.

sn.s: Otra vez no sé la palabra.
sn.e: Again I do not know the word.

sn.s: "¿Y ese chunche cómo se llama?", pregunto.
sn.e: "And what is that chunche called?" I ask.

sn.s: Señalo una cosa en la pared.
sn.e: I point at something on the wall.

sn.s: El señor me dice el nombre.
sn.e: The man tells me the name.

sn.s: Y yo aprendo una palabra más.
sn.e: And I learn one more word.

sn.s: Después le pregunto a Roberto por chunche.
sn.e: Afterwards I ask Roberto about chunche.
"Chunche is any thing," he says.

sn.s: "Si no sabés cómo se llama, es un chunche."
sn.e: "If you don't know what it's called, it's a chunche."
"Pass me that chunche."
"Move that chunche out of the way."

sn.s: "¿Y de dónde viene esa palabra?", pregunto.
sn.e: "And where does that word come from?" I ask.
"I don't know. It's always been said."
There is another word like it: chereque.

sn.s: Un chereque es una cosa vieja.
sn.e: A chereque is an old thing.

sn.s: Un chereque es una cosa que ya no sirve.
sn.e: A chereque is a thing that is no use any more.
"Throw those chereques out," doña Carmen says.

sn.s: Con chunche y cosa uno se salva de todo.
sn.e: With chunche and cosa you get out of anything.

sn.s: No hay que saber la palabra exacta.
sn.e: You do not need to know the exact word.
You need to describe and point.

sn.s: El tamaño, el color, para qué sirve.
sn.e: The size, the colour, what it is for.
That is enough.
People here guess fast.

sn.s: En el mercado hay un puesto que vende solo tornillos.
sn.e: In the market there is a stall that sells nothing but screws.
They are used to explaining things.

sn.s: Arreglo la silla con los clavos.
sn.e: I fix the chair with the nails.
It ends up a bit crooked but it works.

sn.s: Doña Carmen se sienta en ella.
sn.e: Doña Carmen sits on it.
"It works," she says.

sn.s: Y aquí eso es lo importante.
sn.e: And here that is what matters.
